description: To give the students an understanding of the principles behind the latest advances in network technology from the physical to application layer.

syllabus.title: Introduction to IPv6
syllabus.body: IPv6 protocol architecture, addressing, headers, static & automatic address configuration, ICMPv6, neighbor discovery, IPsec, authentication header, encapsulation security payload, transport and tunnel mode, interoperation concepts, dual stack servers, tunnelling and header translation.

syllabus.title: Mobile IP
syllabus.body: Mobile IPv4, mobile IPv6, enhanced/fast handover schemes, network mobility (NEMO), hierarchical mobile IPv6, security in mobile IP, VPN problems & solutions, bidirectional tunneling & route optimization, DHCPv6.

syllabus.title: Software Defined Networking
syllabus.body: SDN background and motivation, SDN data plane and OpenFlow, control plane, application plane, Network Function Virtualization (NFV) architecture and concepts.

syllabus.title: Congestion Control in Wired and Wireless Networks
syllabus.body: TCP congestion control – fairness, scheduling and delay modeling, QoS issues, differentiated services, transport layer in wireless networks, IEEE 802.11a/b/n/g/p, 802.15 standards for wireless.

syllabus.title: IoT and Cloud
syllabus.body: IoT architecture, working with IoT technologies - Bluetooth, Zigbee, BLE and LoRA, CoAP and MQTT, IoT security, cloud system architectures and working with virtualization, cloud security.

outcomes: Understand computer network basics, different models used for study of computer networks, and issues surrounding wired and wireless networks.
Design, calculate, and apply subnet masks to fulfil networking requirements and build routing skills.
Analyse the features and operations of various application layer protocols such as HTTP, DNS, SMTP and FTP.
Analyse the requirements for a given organizational structure and select the most appropriate networking architecture and technologies.
referenceBooks: Youngsong Mun and Hyewon Keren Lee, Understanding IPv6, Springer, 2010.
William Stallings, Foundations of Modern Networking: SDN, NFV, QoE, IoT, and Cloud, 2015.
Rajeev S. Koodli and Charles E. Perkins, Mobile Inter-networking with IPv6, Wiley, 2007.
